summary: Learn to link public spending, indicators, contracts, and outcomes with practical performance-based budgeting tools. Enquire about delivery.
lede: Outcome-based budgeting and performance management helps public finance teams translate policy priorities into budget programmes, cost outputs, select meaningful indicators, and connect appropriations with service-delivery results. It brings planning, costing, implementation, monitoring, and reporting into a practical management system. Through hands-on templates and case data, you will build results chains, budget-performance matrices, indicator reference sheets, expenditure reviews, and data-quality workflows for an IFMIS or equivalent platform. You will also apply the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework, results-based management tools, and contract or performance-agreement scorecards while using recognised performance and fiscal transparency frameworks to assess and communicate results.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for public finance and programme professionals who connect policy priorities, appropriations, implementation evidence, and reform reporting. It suits professionals at beginner to intermediate level who have practical exposure to government budgeting, programme delivery, monitoring and evaluation, or donor-funded public-sector initiatives.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to public budgeting, programme management, monitoring and evaluation, or donor-supported reform reporting. Familiarity with budget classifications, expenditure reports, and basic spreadsheet analysis will help, but advanced economics, programming, or impact-evaluation expertise is not required. Completion requires no coding. Digital and AI-assisted topics remain at operational application level, with dashboard configuration and data review rather than software engineering or production-system deployment.
